summary:
# NOTES: Jimmy Quixote, by Tom Gallon (Hurst and Blackett, 1906; Gutenberg #41754)

Dedication: to Malcolm Watson, "Your friend always, TOM GALLON", London 1906. Author of "Tatterley", "The Golden Thread", "Meg the Lady".

Structure: BOOK I (Ch I–VII), BOOK II (Ch I–IX), BOOK III (Ch I–VI). Ends "THE END". Printed at The Chapel River Press, Kingston, Surrey.

## BOOK I

### Ch I – OLD PAUL'S BABIES
- Old Paul = Paul Nannock, tall, ~light brown thinning hair, high forehead. Returns late July from London to Daisley Cross station (porter says "main glad"). Carries parcels; lost list of purchases. Forgot Jimmy's boots, went back toward station, then realised too late for London.
- Purchases: curtains for study, frocks for Moira (2 inches longer), cricket bat and fishing rod for Jimmy, books/toys/dolls for girls, shawl of many colours for Patience, tobacco for Anthony (full-flavoured; he got the medium by mistake).
- Patience: old woman, scolds, autocrat of house, "Master Paul". Loves Paul; shawl wins her over.
- Anthony Ditchburn: older, rusty black, peevish, nervous hands, wants full-flavoured tobacco. Self-styled scholar, writing a "monumental work".
- Moira: thin dark-eyed girl, ~8–9, hair almost black. Calls him "Old Paul". Sleeps-cheats to come to his room at night ("our sacred hour"). Sayings: "This is the time you belong to me."
- Jimmy: handsome boy ~12–13, "It's been a beastly long day without you, Old Paul."
- Alice (Vickery): fair, blue-eyed, fragile, prim and worldly; visited the Baffalls; "Mr. Baffall saw me home."
- Backstory: Paul Nannock, shy, blushing, rich, drifted in London; fell in love with a dark-eyed woman who loved him three months then left for a richer man. Moved to Daisley Place, Daisley Cross, lived as hermit. Later took child Moira: the woman (her mother) married him and deserted her; on her deathbed she sent for Paul, who took the child.
- Jimmy: parents lost at sea; guardian embezzled, found shot dead in Liverpool hovel. School gave Paul's name as reference.
- Alice: mother, a worldly widow, dumped her with Paul for days/"Paris"; never returned, never heard of again.

### Ch II – AND OLD PAUL'S FRIENDS
- Anthony Ditchburn came in a storm years earlier; stayed. Promised to dedicate his book to Paul. Tobacco supplied by Paul. Opposed Moira's presence ("Send her packing... boarding school"). Paul: "The child stays."
- Tutoring failed: Anthony slept, quoted Horace; Jimmy drew on margins.
- Rev. Temple Purdue: small, mild, spectacled, widower (wife's grave), rector of Daisley Cross, teaches children. Son Charlie Purdue, lonely mischievous boy, same age as Jimmy, teaches them nature.
- Baffalls: Daniel (Mr.) and Flora (Mrs.) Baffall, retired London tradesmen, new house, brand-new carriage. Childless. Mrs. Baffall loves children; Mr. Baffall is grey-bearded, hard-grained, calls wife "mother", had silk hat. Mr. Baffall shook Jimmy's hand. Mrs. Baffall: "I think I should dance, Daniel!"
- Honora Jackman: loud, high voice, single eyeglass, "fine old time", nomad, ~£150 a year, comes to "rusticate" with Baffalls. Schemes to capture Paul. "A rich old bachelor—adopting babies?"

### Ch III – "JIMMY QUIXOTE"
- Honora at dinner party; Paul "exceedingly good". At Paul's house: "Old Paul" explained by Moira. Honora tells Jimmy she has no friend but him; kisses his lips. Jimmy becomes her go-between, reveals the enchanted glade in woods (fir cones, bank, "paradise").
- Honora finds Paul in the glade; Paul sends her back; Jimmy shouts "You're a beast!". Paul: "Poor old Jimmy!... I'll wager... you love her." Jimmy: "I do." Paul calls him "Jimmy Quixote" (knight tilting at windmills). Name sticks.
- Next day Paul agrees to walk Honora through woods.

### Ch IV – THE ELOPING PERSONS
- Moira's jealousy. At 6 am Moira asks: "What do you do when you love anybody?"... "Patience says... you elope." "Somebody who stands between." Plan: elope.
- The Ancient One: aged donkey bought from gipsy (Paul paid bright sovereigns; the gipsy had a swollen face). Chaise bought for 17 shillings from inn stable.
- Provisions: bread, cheese, milk stolen from larder. Breakfast at inn (landlady, round-faced bouncing maid). Ancient One dawdles.
- Patience was once Paul's nurse as a boy when his mother was poor.
- Moira makes Paul promise: "never in all your life will you elope with anybody but me... my very own elopement."
- Return; Honora at gate with eyeglass: "Where have you been hiding all day, you two?" Paul: "We eloped together early this morning."
- Anthony complains Honora "dangerous".

### Ch V – JIMMY'S AFFECTIONS
- Honora leaves; Mrs. Baffall asks Paul to let Honora see children. Honora sings (Irish song). Goes upstairs with Paul's candle to girls' room. Moira feigns sleep. Honora: "I would have sold my immortal soul... to have had you stand beside me." Paul asks her to kiss child; Moira reaches up and embraces Honora.
- Jimmy at station; Honora pays no attention. Letter signed "Honora Jackman... yours ever lovingly"; Jimmy's interest fades.
- Charlie Purdue (tall, fair, reckless) kisses Moira in race to gate. Jimmy jealous; fight with Charlie in wood; Jimmy wins; Charlie: "Say you're sorry", "She is worth it". Moira told Paul; "Oh, wise little woman!"

### Ch VI – MRS. BAFFALL'S DREAM
- Paul goes to London twice, learns he is dying (heart? unspecified illness; "the Presence"; "It's death, Mrs. Baffall."). Night walk, Mrs. Baffall lets him in; he speaks of babies; "Even God sleeps, perhaps". Mrs. Baffall: "I didn't mean 'good-bye'; I meant 'good-night'."

### Ch VII – "OVER THE HILLS AND FAR AWAY"
- Paul dies at foot of stairs, early morning; writes "To Moira, beloved of my heart now and always, I give——" (unfinished). Patience finds him; carries him to his room; locks door. Moira reads note partly; Patience lets her in. "Old Paul—it was kind of you."
- Honora arrives, takes children to woods on funeral day. Funeral: Rev. Temple Purdue, Baffall, Matthew Shandler (man in black, cadaverous, second cousin on father's side, claims estate). No will found.
- Alice to live with Baffalls; Jimmy to London warehouse via Baffall; Moira and Patience to London (Patience's savings; old battered tin trunk).
- Moira and Jimmy part at hilltop in drizzle; "When I come to London I'll look for you." END OF BOOK I.

## BOOK II

### Ch I – THE CALL OF THE WORLD
- Patience and Moira settle in tiny rooms top floor, Chelsea (Locker Street). Four years of loneliness.
- Once Moira goes to opera (Faust) with a rough girl from downstairs.
- Moira writes to Alice, gets reply signed "ALICE VICKERY" (Baffalls moved to London). Moira visits Alice's grand house; Alice cold. Moira seeks Jimmy at warehouse off Cheapside; told he left.

### Ch II – JIMMY—AND A MATTER OF FOOD
- Jimmy's boarding house near Camden Town; shoe fight with weedy youth. Writes stories; editor (flaxen-haired, pipe) and boy William at paper. Pays 16s, guinea; Friday pay. Paper folds. Jimmy dismissed from warehouse. Rooms in small court off Holborn; British Museum reading room; tiny tea shop.

### Ch III – THE COMPLETE LETTER-WRITER
- Patience writes boastful black-edged letter to Baffalls (claims wealth, "investments", "Moira almost too gay"). Baffall sees bluff. Rev. Purdue writes to Charlie suggesting he live with Patience and Moira.
- Anthony Ditchburn, in squalid coffee-house off Fleet Street, begs Purdue for loan; Purdue sends £1 and Charlie's address.
- Charlie visits Moira; she cries "Charlie!"

### Ch IV – THE MAN IN PRINT
- Charlie takes Moira to dinner restaurant, then Bohemia music hall. Takes rooms downstairs in Locker Street. Anthony Ditchburn sleeps on stairs, drinks Charlie's whisky.
- Anthony finds Jimmy at British Museum; Jimmy's story printed. Moira writes Jimmy; Jimmy replies "MY DEAR, DEAR MOIRA... Jimmy".

### Ch V – ANOTHER TASTE OF BOHEMIA
- Moira visits Jimmy's room; he is hungry; she cooks breakfast (rasher and eggs). Landlady (dragon) demands money. Charlie and Anthony arrive. Jimmy receives five-guinea cheque; treats all to lunch.

### Ch VI – CHARLIE PLUNGES
- Charlie's father (Rev. Temple Purdue) confronts Charlie over debts; gives £50 draft and cuts him off. Charlie tries painting, then writing. Charlie proposes to Moira; she loves but uncertain; he says "I love you, Moira... I'll be awfully good to you".

### Ch VII – DREAMS
- Jimmy writes novel; publisher (big-bearded) loses money, owes £6 5s 9d. Bennett Godsby (actor) wants play; Jimmy's synopsis; £20 offered.
- Moira comes to tell Jimmy Charlie asked her to marry him; Jimmy cold: "I cannot see myself ever marrying."

### Ch VIII – THE SIDES OF THE 'BUSES O!
- Play written with Godsby, co-authorship; Godsby garbles press; Mrs. Bennett Godsby tittered. Mrs. Baffall and Alice visit, Alice radiant; invites Jimmy to dine. Name on omnibus.

### Ch IX – THE DAWN
- Play opening night. Moira outside theatre; sees Alice enter, fails to get seat. Goes to Charlie's room; Charlie sleeps; she returns, lies on his sofa crying "Jimmy—you might have remembered". Charlie wakes, takes advantage; "I want love to-night!" Dawn; she flees sobbing. END OF BOOK II.

## BOOK III

### Ch I – "IT'LL BE ALL RIGHT"
- Moira shames; avoids Charlie. Charlie debts; borrows from Patience (she refuses unless she speaks to Moira). Moira tells Charlie she's pregnant; he says "It'll be all right." Patience comforts Moira.
- Charlie goes to father; father refuses: "Get out of my house." Charlie crosses road in London, hit by horses; dying, asks for Jimmy, sends message "it'd be all right".

### Ch II – JIMMY QUIXOTE
- Jimmy successful; rich; Society with Baffalls and Alice; Ashby Feak (rival, explorer).
- Charlie dying: confesses wrong; Jimmy promises marry Moira. "Tell her... I said it'd be all right."
- Patience: Moira had gone. Rev. Purdue comes to Jimmy. Jimmy says "She will be provided for."
- Jimmy tells Moira he'll marry her; she accepts. "Exactly as before."

### Ch III – TWO WAYS OF LOVE
- Wedding in rain, shadow of the dead. Moira returns money; Moira in country with Patience and baby (Moira, dark-eyed, born after Charlie's death, daughter).
- Jimmy engaged to Alice, secretly. Ashby Feak visits; Moira comes to Jimmy's rooms; Feak learns she is Jimmy's wife. Jimmy: "Yes—there is someone else." (Alice.)

### Ch IV – THE LONG NIGHT
- Anthony Ditchburn returns, finds Moira at Daisley Cross, steals her letters (unsent, addressed "James Larrance, Esq.") from box; takes to Jimmy. Jimmy drinks heavily, hurt, rejects; Anthony paid £5.
- Jimmy's memories: he had tried to strangle Moira in madness; she smiled "Yes—kill me." She nursed him; he wrote.

### Ch V – "IF I MIGHT DIE!"
- Moira refuses Jimmy's offer for pity: "I will live with my child alone."
- Jimmy reads letters: "I LOVE YOU"; "The child is yours!"; "If I might die, Jimmy dear——"
- Anthony tells Moira what he did; she orders him out. Moira leaves, saying "Never!" then to Patience. 

### Ch VI – THE SPIRIT OF OLD PAUL
- Jimmy takes baby, leaves note: "I have taken the child... JIMMY." Goes to Daisley Cross with Patience. Moira follows, watches him at inn speak to baby about Old Paul and childhood; "I love you, Moira." She kneels at Old Paul's grave; Jimmy finds her; "You like the baby?" "She's mine—my baby; you said so."
- Ending: reconciliation under autumn moon; Patience weeps happily. "Love had shown them the way... into the brighter promise of a new day." THE END.
